question: Does Physics 1 count for a gen ed? I'm a bio major and trying to figure out if I can double dip it with my major requirements.
answer:
Yes. Physics I courses count for Gen Ed 18—Scientific Reasoning (GESR): PHYS 111 [4], PHYS 116 [5], and PHYS 116L [6, 19]. [19] lists Biology BS among the catalog’s bachelor’s majors. For Biology BS, PHYS 111 and PHYS 118L are required; the Biology major requirements do not list PHYS 116/116L. [3] General Education courses may double count toward a major, but no more than two Gen Ed courses may do so. [9] So PHYS 111 appears to satisfy both the Biology major requirement and Scientific Reasoning; the catalog allows that double count, subject to the two-course limit. [3, 9] PHYS 111 is 4 credits and has a corequisite: enroll in PHYS 118L INTRODUCTORY PHYSICS I LAB. [4]

Sources: [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BIOL) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHYS111) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PHYS116) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [19](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: what upper level electives are required for the math major, and do i need to take abstract algebra or real analysis or both
answer:
The catalog lists Mathematics BS (Bachelor of Science) as the math major [15].

For the Traditional Track, choose at least 4 electives from MATH 239 Graph Theory, 240 Cryptography, 245 Numerical Analysis, 253 Probability, 282 Number Theory, 290 Topics, 321 Geometry, 339 Complex Variables, 370 Applied Statistics or 353 Statistics, 360 Stochastic Calculus for Finance, 390 Advanced Topics, and 490 Topics. At least 2 electives must be 300- or 400-level [1].

For the Teacher Education Track, choose at least 1 elective from MATH 239 Graph Theory, 240 Cryptography, 245 Numerical Analysis, 290 Topics, 305 Differential Equations, 339 Complex Variables, 360 Stochastic Calculus for Finance, 390 Advanced Topics, and 490 Topics. The listed requirements do not specify an upper-level minimum for this track [1].

You need both: MATH 416 Introduction to Analysis and MATH 432 Abstract Algebra are required courses in both tracks [1]. MATH 432 is 4 credits, has the WRITING INTENSIVE (WRIT) attribute, and requires CRWT 102 Critical Reading and Writing II or CRWT 102S Critical Reading and Writing II, and MATH 262 Linear Algebra [2].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-MATH) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/MATH432) [15](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: I'm a junior in environmental science. What courses are supposed to be taken junior and senior year in the recommended sequence, and when is the capstone?
answer:
The Environmental Science recommended plan is for students admitted to the major during the 2023–2024 academic year. [1]

**Third year (junior):** Fall: Distribution Category (choose 1)—Culture and Creativity, Systems, Sustainability and Society, or Values and Ethics; ENSC 343 Environmental Chemistry Lecture; ENSC 343L Environmental Chemistry Lab; ENSC Elective 1. Total 14 credits. Spring: ENSC 345 Research Design & Statistics; GEOL 328 Paleontology, Paleoecology & Paleoenvironments Lecture; GEOL 328L Paleontology, Paleoecology & Paleoenvironments Lab; ENSC 225 GIS for Environmental Science; Distribution Category (choose 1)—Culture and Creativity, Systems, Sustainability and Society, or Values and Ethics (must be outside of TAS). Total 17.5 credits. [1]

**Fourth year (senior):** Fall: ENSC 417 Ecological Field Research Lecture; ENSC 417L Ecological Field Research Lab; ENSC Major Elective 2; Elective; Elective. Total 18 credits. Spring: ENSC Major Elective 3; Elective; Elective; Elective. Total 16 credits. [1]

The plan lists ENSC 417 and its lab in fourth-year fall, but does not identify them as a capstone or state when a capstone occurs. I don’t have verified information about capstone timing. Contact the School of Science, Nursing, and Health Office: SNHOffice@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7734, ASB-422.

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-ENSC)
